principle: Crash frequency, pedestrian exposure, vehicle exposure and contextual covariates are distinct analytical concepts and must not be collapsed by convenience.

direct_measure.current_evidence: ATU publicly documents 24-hour, seven-day people and vehicle counts at 27 high-traffic points for PMU work, but reusable citywide microdata has not been qualified.

local_validation_signal.semantics: observed transit demand at Metropolitano stations/corridor

proxy_policy.rule: Proxy components remain covariates unless a separately validated exposure model is demonstrated.
validation_requirements: held-out local validation where sample size permits
no use as a count-model offset unless ratio-scale exposure semantics are independently proven

direct_measure.current_evidence: PMU work proves direct traffic/person counting was performed at selected points; a reusable network-wide aligned volume source remains unqualified.

vehicle_exposure.rule: Route geometry, congestion classes and toll-station counts are not interchangeable with citywide vehicle exposure.

fallback_product_semantics.if_direct_exposure_remains_unavailable: Train and evaluate crash-frequency/occurrence models with qualified contextual covariates; present results as model-estimated relative analytical risk/frequency, not as exposure-normalized individual collision probability.
fallback_product_semantics.forbidden_claim: Do not label a crash-frequency model as an exposure-normalized pedestrian risk rate.

exit_conditions: Direct pedestrian exposure is qualified, or the proxy strategy is explicitly selected and validated for its limited semantics.
Vehicle exposure treatment is documented separately from route/context geometry.
Product wording matches the selected target semantics.
The benchmark plan includes an ablation without exposure proxies and without lagged outcome history.
